messages:
Alex: Quick profiling dump from last night's canary. Pre-fill is dominating some routes: prefill ~65% of wall time, decode ~35%. p95 ~120ms, p99 ~420ms, but we see 1–2% of requests hitting 800–1200ms. Microbatch avg=8, when we bump to 16 throughput +22% but p99 jumps ~2x.

Ben: Can you paste the profiler output? curious about kernel hot paths and whether prefill is spending time on kv lookups or slow kernels.

Alex: pasted snippet:```
route: /v1/generate
-- prefill: 0.65
   kernels: matmul_1 (42%), kv_lookup (18%), softmax (5%)
-- decode: 0.35
   kernels: cross_attn (30%), matmul_2 (25%), tok_sampling (10%)
p95: 120ms, p99: 420ms
long-tail count: 1.4% > 800ms
microbatch_size: 8 (sigma 3)
```

Cheng: Looks like two things: slow matmul kernel on long sequences and KV misses during prefill. Are these long prompts or many short requests batched?

Alex: Mostly mixed workload. 60% short prompts (<64 tokens) and 40% long (>512). The long ones dominate matmul time but the tail spikes are short requests that get microbatched with long sequences.

Maria: That's the classic latency SLO vs throughput tradeoff. If we let scheduler batch strictly by arrival time, short requests suffer when grouped with long ones. We should try adaptive microbatch sizing + fast-path routing for short sequences.

Ben: Proposal: two routing lanes: "short" (<=64) with microbatch max 6 and aggressive prefills disabled, "long" with microbatch max 24 and kv-prefetch on. Router picks lane by promised sequence length in header. This reduces head-of-line blocking.

Cheng: Agree. Also add kernel selection hint: for short lane pick low-latency small-matmul kernels (fp16 friendly) and avoid quantized fallback that's slower on tiny batches. For long lane prefer throughput kernels and enable KV prefetch.

Alex: Quick pseudocode for router config:```json
{"lanes": [ {"name":"short","max_batch":6,"kernel_hint":"low_latency"}, {"name":"long","max_batch":24,"kernel_hint":"high_throughput","kv_prefetch":true} ] }
```

Maria: We should be careful: short lane mustn't starve GPU. Add a soft quota and time-based flush (e.g., flush after 8ms or when batch >=3). Also measure p50/p95 after change.

Ben: Also we can try dynamic microbatch sizing: start with small target, if GPU utilization <60% enlarge batches over 200ms windows. That gives best-effort throughput without harming SLOs.

Cheng: What's the plan to confirm KV is the other culprit? We need a metric: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss[5m])) by (route)` and a trace sample for a tail request. Alex can you attach flamegraph of a 900ms request?

Alex: attaching short trace below (inline):```
trace: request 0xabc
prefill: 580ms (matmul 320ms, kv_lookup 180ms, copy 80ms)
decode: 260ms (cross_attn 140ms)
notes: kv_lookup had 3x cache miss rate vs baseline
```

infra-bot: canary-deploy #r123 applied to cluster-7 at 2003456700. No infra-level alerts.

Maria: Action items: 1) Alex/Cheng - implement lane router and per-lane kernel hints, instrument p50/p95/p99 by lane. 2) Ben - add auto-resize heuristic on microbatch with GPU util feedback. 3) Alex - run targeted KV warmers for hot prefixes and add `kv_cache_miss` alert. 4) Run 24h canary, collect tail traces, compare p99.

Ben: Also add an experiment flag `runtime.routing.experimental_adaptive=true` so we can toggle quickly.

Alex: I'll start a branch and post the canary config. Goal: reduce short-request p99 by >=40% with <=5% throughput regression.

Cheng: If this works, follow-up: kernel selection policy could be ML-driven (predict optimal kernel based on seq_len + batch_size + topology). But first, baseline heuristics.

Maria: :thumbsup: Keep thread updated with perf numbers and one example flamegraph for a fixed time window.

Alex: Will do. Posting initial PR and canary plan within today.
